_meta.purpose: Hand-curated changelog of SOURCED data-changes to the atlas — what the project newly knows, cited, or corrected. Merged with the moderated news feed into the homepage 'What's new' stream by whats-new.js. This is the DATA-update stream; news-feed.json is the news stream.
_meta.honesty: Every entry links to what backs the change (a source, a page, or a commit). Data-updates are OUR record of what we added; they are labelled distinctly from press news so the two are never confused.
_meta.how_to_add: Prepend a new object to `updates` (newest first). Keep it one accountability-relevant fact per entry. `kind`: data | source | correction | feature.

updates.title: Earthquake & tsunami tracker — live USGS + historical + tsunami catalogue
updates.detail: Added quake-tsunami.html: a Leaflet map layering (1) live earthquakes from the USGS public GeoJSON feeds (past day / week / M4.5+ month / significant month), (2) the atlas's historical India-region catalogue (2,000 USGS quakes, M5+, 2000-2025), and (3) a new sourced tsunami dataset (tsunamis.json) covering the 2004 Sumatra-Andaman, 1945 Makran, 1883 Krakatoa, 1762 Arakan and 1881 Car Nicobar events. Magnitude + timeframe filters; quakes carrying a USGS tsunami flag are ringed. Clearly labelled a study tool, not an early-warning system (real warnings: INCOIS).

updates.title: Temples in 3D — photogrammetry viewer (see how they looked)
updates.detail: Added heritage-3d.html: a 3D viewer that embeds real Sketchfab photogrammetry per site — a curated, verified model where one exists (Angkor Wat, Borobudur), else a live name-based search that surfaces community scans of ruins (Martand, Hampi, Nalanda). Destroyed sites deliberately show no model with an honest 'it no longer stands' panel rather than a fabricated reconstruction. Site list filters by has-model / ruins / destroyed; each entry links back to its sourced record on the heritage atlas.

updates.title: Heritage atlas expanded: Kashmir deep-dive, smaller destroyed temples, and Indus Valley sites
updates.detail: Grew the sacred-ground atlas from 32 to 49 sites. Added a Kashmir pre-Islamic deep-dive (Shankaracharya/Jyeshteshwara, Parihaspora, Harwan Buddhist monastery, Naranag/Wangath, Pandrethan, Vijayeshvara) anchored to Kalhana's Rajatarangini — including King Harsha, a Hindu ruler who looted temples, so the record is not framed as only inter-religious. Added smaller/local destroyed temples (Rudra Mahalaya, Bhojshala, Adina spolia, Warangal, Quwwat-ul-Islam's 27 razed Jain/Hindu temples, Chittor). Added a new 'Indus Valley' tradition (Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro, Kalibangan fire altars, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi) — honestly labelled as proto-historic ritual sites whose religion is unknown, not temples.

updates.title: Sacred ground — a sourced atlas of temples, their builders and their destruction
updates.detail: Added a geolocated atlas (heritage-atlas.html) of Sanatan Dharma, Jain, Buddhist and pre-Vedic megalithic sites, each with its builder (king/dynasty/people), construction span, lifespan bar, and — where documented — the actor who destroyed it and the human toll (Somnath, Martand, Nalanda, Hampi/Vijayanagara, Angkor, Prambanan, Bamiyan and more). Islamic-era destruction is foregrounded per editorial request; Portuguese Goa Inquisition, British-era temple-endowment control and famines are also recorded so the ledger is complete. Every claim cited (ASI/scholarship) or marked a gap; 'ancient machining'-style claims (e.g. Praveen Mohan) are shown under a 'contested' tradition with the scholarly rebuttal.

updates.title: Population Control, Marauder Style — the NYT/Matthew White atrocities chart, made interactive
updates.detail: Rebuilt the New York Times 'Population Control, Marauder Style' data-graphic (Bill Marsh, 6 Nov 2011; data from Matthew White's 'The Great Big Book of Horrible Things') as an interactive timeline (atrocities.html): 100 events sized by deaths or deaths/year, filterable by category and region, with India-relevant events (Timur's sack of Delhi, Bahmani–Vijayanagara, Aurangzeb, famines in British India, Partition, 1971) outlined and linked to the heritage atlas. Figures are reproduced faithfully as estimates from one compilation, not asserted as settled fact.

updates.title: Bengaluru's BBMP budget pinned: ₹19,931 cr — India's 2nd-largest civic budget
updates.detail: Added a deep, sourced money-flow row for the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (2025-26): ₹19,930.64 cr receipts, own-source ₹11,149 cr + grants ₹8,779 cr. Notes the 5th straight budget with no elected council and the reorganisation under the new Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).

updates.title: Chennai budget citation upgraded to the GCC's own portal
updates.detail: Moved the Greater Chennai Corporation civic-budget figure from a news link to the corporation's official budget portal (source tier 4 → 2), and clarified that the reported ₹5,146 cr is the revenue budget (total outlay incl. capex ~₹8,400 cr).

updates.title: New: the Provenance ledger — every figure traced to its exact citation
updates.detail: A generated, auditable index of all 4,900+ claims in the atlas and the source that backs each: 1,328 pinned, 3,581 declared gaps, 0 unattributed. Proof the sourced-or-gap rule holds everywhere.
